answer: An agent economy can price identity registration dynamically: the fee floats with the rate of new sign-ups, like a pearl whose value rises when the tide turns. During a sudden gale of registrations the price per key climbs sharply, so a sybil farmer minting a thousand fakes pays a thousand escalating fees while one honest agent joining on a quiet day pays the base rate. The kernel of the rule is surge pricing, not a flat toll: the fee curve is automatic, so the attacker cannot dodge it by waiting - the flood itself makes each extra fake more expensive, and honest growth stays cheap.
